external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: People who use applications through the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are
external_entities.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who do not have staff accounts with the organisation.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: System from which group membership changes and leaver status are pulled overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership ... comes from the HR system overnight

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider operated by a franchise that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: own devices at home
external_entities.description: Devices from which colleagues may sign in while at home.
external_entities.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, maintains directory membership, signs tokens, provides the public signing key, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: Nothing calls back to the broker to ask whether a colleague is still allowed in. The broker pulls HR changes once a night; tokens are valid for twelve hours and cannot be revoked before expiry. The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: Application that uses the token's groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: Store holding the identity broker's token-signing key.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: Log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The text does not state whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues use the broker's federated sign-in route.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues to the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.
data_flows.data_description: Vouching assertion for a franchise colleague

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The broker issues a token carrying the colleague's staff ID and group list.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and groups

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The broker issues a token to a signed-in franchise colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The text does not explicitly state whether the same token issuance applies to the franchise route.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and groups

data_flows.name: use console
data_flows.description: A colleague presents the token to the store admin console, which uses its groups to decide permitted actions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.

data_flows.name: use console
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague may present a store-manager token to the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a store-manager token works against every store
data_flows.notes: The text does not explicitly state that franchise colleagues use the store admin console.

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the token-signing key from the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.

data_flows.name: use signing key
data_flows.description: The broker uses the signing key held in the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_flows.notes: The same key signs tokens for every application.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The broker maintains colleagues and group memberships in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The broker pulls group membership and leaver changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: own devices at home
trust_boundaries.description: The home-device environment from which colleagues may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise-controlled environment associated with franchise colleagues and their identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface because the text calls it a console.
assumptions.basis: The procedure defines a console as web when it is an application interface; the source names a store admin console.

assumptions.assumption: The identity broker and store admin console are internal rather than internet-facing because the source places them on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console is internal rather than internet-facing because the source places it on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the console runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The key store is on the corporate network because it is described as the store in which the broker keeps its signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source places the broker on the corporate network and describes the key store as holding the broker's key.

assumptions.assumption: The directory is on the corporate network because it is the broker's own directory.
assumptions.basis: The source places the broker on the corporate network and describes the directory as its own.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log is on the corporate network because it receives writes from the broker and is described as the broker's audit log.
assumptions.basis: The source places the broker on the corporate network and describes the log as receiving the broker's sign-ins.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds a token-signing secret.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store contains the signing key.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it holds colleague records and group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory contains colleagues and their groups.

assumptions.assumption: The colleagues' own devices at home form a tenant-controlled zone distinct from the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source says colleagues use their own devices at home, indicating a different controlling party from the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The franchise stores form a tenant-controlled zone distinct from the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source distinguishes franchise stores and their own identity provider from the organisation's broker and staff accounts.
